subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was notified in 2006 and-

options.A: provides the first ever legal framework for recognition of the concept of enterprise, comprising both manufacturing and service entities
options.B: provides the first ever legal framework for the small scale sector, but is confined to entities engaged in manufacture or production
options.C: replaced the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 so far as that Act applied to industrial undertakings in India
options.D: applies only to enterprises which have obtained a registration certificate from the Central Government before commencing business

answer_html:
Answer: (A) provides the first ever legal framework for recognition of the concept of enterprise, comprising both manufacturing and service entities.

The Act was notified in 2006 to address the policy issues affecting micro, small and medium enterprises as well as the coverage and investment ceiling of the sector. It provides the first ever legal framework for recognition of the concept of enterprise, which comprises both manufacturing and service entities, and it also provides a statutory consultative mechanism with a wide range of advisory functions.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The primary responsibility for the promotion and development of micro, small and medium enterprises rests with-

options.A: the Central Government, the State Governments supplementing its efforts
options.B: the Reserve Bank of India, acting through the scheduled commercial banks
options.C: the National Small Industries Corporation, acting through its zonal offices
options.D: the State Governments, the Central Government supplementing their efforts

answer_html:
Answer: (D) the State Governments, the Central Government supplementing their efforts.

The primary responsibility of the promotion and development of micro, small and medium enterprises is that of the State Governments. The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and its organisations assist the States in their efforts to encourage entrepreneurship, employment and livelihood opportunities and to enhance the competitiveness of these enterprises.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under the revised classification applicable with effect from 1 July 2020, an enterprise is classified as a small enterprise where-

options.A: its investment in plant and machinery or equipment is not more than ₹50 crore and its annual turnover is not more than ₹250 crore
options.B: its investment in plant and machinery or equipment is not more than ₹10 crore, whatever the amount of its annual turnover may be
options.C: its investment in plant and machinery or equipment is not more than ₹10 crore and its annual turnover is not more than ₹50 crore
options.D: its investment in plant and machinery or equipment is not more than ₹1 crore and its annual turnover is not more than ₹5 crore

answer_html:
Answer: (C) its investment in plant and machinery or equipment is not more than ₹10 crore and its annual turnover is not more than ₹50 crore.

The revised classification applies a composite criterion of investment in plant and machinery or equipment together with annual turnover, and the same table applies to manufacturing enterprises and to enterprises rendering services. A micro enterprise has investment of not more than ₹1 crore and turnover of not more than ₹5 crore; a small enterprise, investment of not more than ₹10 crore and turnover of not more than ₹50 crore; and a medium enterprise, investment of not more than ₹50 crore and turnover of not more than ₹250 crore.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: For the purpose of classifying an enterprise-

options.A: the investment is taken at the original cost of acquisition of the assets, without any statutory linkage
options.B: the investment is linked to the income tax return of the previous year, and otherwise rests on self declaration
options.C: the investment is linked to the audited balance sheet of the current year, and self declaration is not accepted
options.D: the investment is certified by the District Industries Centre before the classification takes effect at all

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the investment is linked to the income tax return of the previous year, and otherwise rests on self declaration.

The calculation of investment in plant and machinery or equipment is linked to the income tax return of the previous year, and otherwise proceeds on self declaration. Assets of a tangible nature form part of plant and machinery other than land and furniture and fittings. While calculating turnover, exports are excluded and the information is linked to the income tax and goods and services tax returns.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Vaitarna Rubber Products is a proprietorship concern manufacturing moulded rubber components. Its accounts for the year show the following.

The tangible assets of the enterprise stand in its books at ₹9.2 crore, of which land accounts for ₹1.0 crore and furniture and fittings for ₹0.2 crore; the balance is plant and machinery.

Its annual turnover for the year is ₹42 crore, which includes export turnover of ₹6 crore.

The proprietor wishes to know how the enterprise is classified under the revised criteria applicable with effect from 1 July 2020.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. The investment in plant and machinery to be reckoned for classifying Vaitarna Rubber Products is-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) ₹8.0 crore.

Assets of a tangible nature form part of plant and machinery other than land and furniture and fittings. From the tangible assets of ₹9.2 crore, the land of ₹1.0 crore and the furniture and fittings of ₹0.2 crore are therefore left out, leaving ₹8.0 crore. Taking the whole of the tangible assets gives ₹9.2 crore, leaving out the land alone gives ₹8.2 crore, and leaving out the furniture and fittings alone gives ₹9.0 crore.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Vaitarna Rubber Products is a proprietorship concern manufacturing moulded rubber components. Its accounts for the year show the following.

The tangible assets of the enterprise stand in its books at ₹9.2 crore, of which land accounts for ₹1.0 crore and furniture and fittings for ₹0.2 crore; the balance is plant and machinery.

Its annual turnover for the year is ₹42 crore, which includes export turnover of ₹6 crore.

The proprietor wishes to know how the enterprise is classified under the revised criteria applicable with effect from 1 July 2020.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. In a later year the turnover of the enterprise rises to ₹60 crore, its investment remaining unchanged. The position then is that-

options.A: it moves to the medium category, and loses with immediate effect every benefit which it enjoyed as a small enterprise
options.B: it remains a small enterprise, because the investment in plant and machinery has not changed during the year
options.C: it falls outside the definition altogether, the turnover having crossed the ceiling for a small enterprise
options.D: it moves to the medium category, but continues to avail the non-tax benefit it was originally entitled to for the next 3 years

answer_html:
Answer: (D) it moves to the medium category, but continues to avail the non-tax benefit it was originally entitled to for the next 3 years.

The composite criterion is applied afresh. Investment of ₹8.0 crore and turnover of ₹60 crore are both within the medium limits of ₹50 crore and ₹250 crore, but the turnover now exceeds the ₹50 crore ceiling for a small enterprise, so the unit graduates to the medium category. Where in the course of doing business a unit goes to the next category, or goes out of the purview altogether, it continues to avail the non-tax benefit it was originally entitled to for the next 3 years from coming into the next category.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The highest executive body for the formulation of policies and the administration of the rules, regulations and laws relating to micro, small and medium enterprises in India is-

options.A: the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
options.B: the Ministry of Industry and Commerce of the Union
options.C: the National Small Industries Corporation Limited
options.D: the Small Industries Development Bank of India

answer_html:
Answer: (A) the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises is a branch of the Government of India and is the highest executive body for the formulation of policies and the administration of the rules, regulations and laws relating to micro, small and medium enterprises. The Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Agro and Rural Industries was created in October 1999 and was split in September 2001 into two ministries, which were later merged into the single Ministry.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has its head office at Delhi and its ex-officio Chairperson is-

options.A: an officer of the Reserve Bank not below the rank of an Executive Director of the Bank
options.B: the Minister in charge of the Ministry having administrative control of the enterprises
options.C: the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry having administrative control
options.D: the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Small Industries Development Bank

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the Minister in charge of the Ministry having administrative control of the enterprises.

The Central Government has established the National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises with its head office at Delhi. The Minister in charge of the Ministry or Department of the Central Government having administrative control of these enterprises is the ex-officio Chairperson, and the Minister of State or Deputy Minister in that Ministry is the ex officio Vice-Chairperson. The Secretary chairs the Advisory Committee, not the Board.

question_html: The National Small Industries Corporation Limited, whose main function is to promote, aid and foster the growth of micro and small enterprises generally on a commercial basis, was established in-

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: For the purposes of the delayed payment provisions of the Act, a supplier is-

options.A: any enterprise which supplies goods or renders services to a buyer for consideration, however classified
options.B: a micro or small enterprise, whether or not it has filed a memorandum with the authority so referred to
options.C: a micro or small enterprise which has filed a memorandum with the authority referred to in Section 8(1)
options.D: a micro, small or medium enterprise which has filed a memorandum with the authority so referred to

answer_html:
Answer: (C) a micro or small enterprise which has filed a memorandum with the authority referred to in Section 8(1).

Supplier means a micro or small enterprise which has filed a memorandum with the authority referred to in sub-section (1) of Section 8. A medium enterprise is therefore not a supplier, and the delayed payment protection of the Act does not extend to it. Buyer, in contrast, means whoever buys any goods or receives any services from a supplier for consideration.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The appointed day means the day following immediately after the expiry of-

options.A: thirty days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance of any goods or services
options.B: forty-five days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance of the goods or services
options.C: sixty days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance of any goods or services
options.D: fifteen days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance of any goods or services

answer_html:
Answer: (D) fifteen days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance of any goods or services.

The appointed day is the day following immediately after the expiry of the period of fifteen days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance. The day of acceptance is the day of actual delivery of goods or rendering of services, or, where the buyer objects in writing within fifteen days of that day, the day on which the objection is removed by the supplier. Where no objection is made in writing within 15 days, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery or rendering.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Where the buyer fails to make payment to a supplier within the time allowed, he is liable to pay-

options.A: simple interest at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank for the period of delay
options.B: compound interest with quarterly rests at the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: compound interest with monthly rests at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank
options.D: compound interest with monthly rests at two times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank

answer_html:
Answer: (C) compound interest with monthly rests at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank.

The buyer is liable to pay compound interest with monthly rests to the supplier on the amount, from the appointed day or, as the case may be, from the date immediately following the date agreed upon, at three times of the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank. A company whose payment is due for 45 days or more from the date of acceptance of the goods or services must also submit a half-yearly return to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under Section 8 the filing of a memorandum with the authority specified by the State Government is-

options.A: at the discretion of every enterprise, the memorandum being merely a record for statistical purposes maintained by the State Government
options.B: at the discretion of a micro or small enterprise and of a medium enterprise rendering services, but mandatory for a medium enterprise manufacturing goods
options.C: mandatory for a micro or small enterprise and for a medium enterprise rendering services, but at the discretion of a medium enterprise manufacturing goods
options.D: mandatory for every enterprise which proposes to carry on business as a micro, small or medium enterprise, whatever the activity it carries on

answer_html:
Answer: (B) at the discretion of a micro or small enterprise and of a medium enterprise rendering services, but mandatory for a medium enterprise manufacturing goods.

A person intending to establish a micro or small enterprise, and a medium enterprise engaged in providing or rendering services, may file the memorandum at his discretion; a medium enterprise engaged in the manufacture or production of goods shall file it. The memorandum goes to such authority as may be specified by the State Government. No licence is required from the Central Government to start such an enterprise.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A reference made to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council-

options.A: may be made only by the buyer, and shall be decided within a period of 45 days from the date of making it
options.B: may be made by any party to the dispute, and shall be decided within a period of 90 days from the date of making it
options.C: may be made only by the supplier, and shall be decided within a period of 90 days from the date of making it
options.D: may be made by any party to the dispute, and shall be decided within a period of 180 days from that date

answer_html:
Answer: (B) may be made by any party to the dispute, and shall be decided within a period of 90 days from the date of making it.

Any party to a dispute may, with regard to any amount due under Section 17, make a reference to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council, and every reference so made shall be decided within a period of 90 days from the date of making the reference. The Council, or the centre providing alternate dispute resolution services, has jurisdiction to act as arbitrator or conciliator in a dispute between a supplier located within its jurisdiction and a buyer located anywhere in India.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Advisory Committee constituted by the Central Government consists of-

options.A: the Secretary to the Government of India as Chairperson, not more than five officers of the Central Government and not more than three representatives of the State Governments
options.B: the Minister in charge as Chairperson, not more than five officers of the Central Government and not more than three representatives of the State Governments, all ex officio
options.C: the Secretary to the Government of India as Chairperson, not more than three officers of the Central Government and not more than five representatives of the State Governments
options.D: the Chairman of the National Board as Chairperson, together with such officers and representatives as the Central Government may from time to time appoint

answer_html:
Answer: (A) the Secretary to the Government of India as Chairperson, not more than five officers of the Central Government and not more than three representatives of the State Governments.

The Advisory Committee consists of the Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry or Department having administrative control of the enterprises as Chairperson ex-officio, not more than five officers of the Central Government possessing the necessary expertise, not more than three representatives of the State Governments, and one representative each of the associations of micro, small and medium enterprises, all ex officio. The Member-Secretary of the Board is also the ex officio Member-Secretary of the Advisory Committee.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: As regards the National Board for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises-

options.A: three Members of Parliament sit on it, one elected by the House of the People and two by the Council of States, and it meets at least once in every six months
options.B: five Members of Parliament sit on it, three elected by the House of the People and two by the Council of States, and it meets at least once in every three months
options.C: two Members of Parliament sit on it, one elected by the House of the People and one by the Council of States, and it meets at least once in every calendar year
options.D: three Members of Parliament sit on it, two elected by the House of the People and one by the Council of States, and it meets at least once in every three months

answer_html:
Answer: (D) three Members of Parliament sit on it, two elected by the House of the People and one by the Council of States, and it meets at least once in every three months.

The Board includes three Members of Parliament, of whom two are elected by the House of the People and one by the Council of States, and it shall meet at least once in every three months. Among its other members are six Ministers of the State Governments, four Secretaries to the Government of India, twenty persons representing associations of these enterprises including not less than 3 representing associations of women's enterprises, three persons of eminence not less than one of whom shall be a woman, and two representatives of Central Trade Union Organisations.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Where the conciliation initiated on a reference to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council is not successful and stands terminated without any settlement, the Council-

options.A: shall refer the parties to the civil court having jurisdiction, its own authority being exhausted on the failure of conciliation
options.B: shall record the failure and close the reference, the supplier being left to pursue such remedy as may be open to it
options.C: shall refer the dispute to the National Board, which alone may take up a failed conciliation for arbitration
options.D: shall itself take up the dispute for arbitration, the Council consisting of not less than three but not more than five members

answer_html:
Answer: (D) shall itself take up the dispute for arbitration, the Council consisting of not less than three but not more than five members.

On receipt of a reference the Council shall either itself conduct conciliation or seek the assistance of an institution or centre providing alternate dispute resolution services. Where the conciliation is not successful and stands terminated without any settlement between the parties, the Council shall itself take up the dispute for arbitration. The Council is established by the State Government by notification and consists of not less than three but not more than five members drawn from the specified categories, including the Director of Industries or an officer not below that rank.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Where a buyer is required to get his annual accounts audited under any law for the time being in force, he must furnish in his annual statement of accounts the principal amount and the interest due thereon remaining unpaid to any supplier at the end of each accounting year. That interest-

options.A: need be disclosed only where the buyer is a company, and is allowed as a deduction from income
options.B: must be shown separately from the principal amount, and is not allowed as a deduction from income
options.C: must be shown separately from the principal amount, but is allowed as a deduction from income
options.D: may be shown together with the principal amount, and is not allowed as a deduction from income

answer_html:
Answer: (B) must be shown separately from the principal amount, and is not allowed as a deduction from income.

Section 22 requires a buyer whose accounts are audited to furnish, in his annual statement of accounts, the principal amount and the interest due thereon, to be shown separately, remaining unpaid to any supplier as at the end of each accounting year. The interest payable or paid under the Act is not allowed as a deduction from income.
